title: What happens if you flush a toilet during a power outage?

lines.text: When the electricity suddenly goes out in your house, can you still safely flush your toilet?
lines.caps: Can you flush the *toilet | during a | *power outage?

lines.text: The surprising answer depends entirely on where your water comes from.
lines.caps: The answer depends | entirely on your *water | *system

lines.text: If you live in a city connected to municipal gravity water towers, your toilet will flush normally.
lines.caps: City water towers use *gravity | and flush *normally

lines.text: Standard gravity toilets rely on mechanical siphons, requiring zero electricity inside your home.
However, if your home relies on an electric well pump or basement sewage ejector, you have exactly one flush.
lines.caps: Well pumps and *septic pumps | stop working | *instantly

lines.text: Once the tank empties, it won't refill, and using it further risks backing up raw sewage.
lines.caps: Flushing again can *back up | sewage into your *home!

lines.text: In an extended blackout, keep buckets of water handy to manually pour flush your bowl.
lines.caps: Pour a bucket of *water | to manually flush!
